prompt:
Produce up to 4 distinct, useful design or engineering actions for the task below. Explore materially different mechanisms, including non-obvious alternatives. Respect every constraint. Give executable changes in the target domain, with an implementation step and a falsifiable check. Do not claim unmeasured gains, invent supporting facts, or rename the same action several ways. State actions in the user's terms; omit donor names and analogy explanations from the answer. Fewer actions, including none, are acceptable when no additional valid action remains. Keep each action compact: aim for 60–80 words TOTAL across its five fields, never more than 110. Suggested field budgets: action 8 words, mechanism 16, implementation 22, check 20, risk 10. The 110-word maximum applies to the SUM of all five values, not to each field.

Task:
{
  "title": "Prevent large jobs from starving small jobs",
  "brief": "A single worker pool processes image transforms. Jobs require between one and sixty seconds. A few customers submit hundreds of long jobs, delaying occasional short jobs from other customers.",
  "constraints": [
    "Twelve workers are fixed; no autoscaling or preemption of an in-progress transform.",
    "Runtime estimates based on file size are imperfect.",
    "Each customer must eventually make progress even under sustained arrivals from others.",
    "Queue metadata may store per-customer counters and the last 100 completed runtimes."
  ],
  "success_criteria": [
    "Bound a fairness objective and distinguish it from mean latency.",
    "Small jobs gain opportunities without permanently blocking large jobs.",
    "Specify a workload test with inaccurate estimates and a continuous heavy customer."
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Changing transform quality or rejecting every long job."
  ]
}
Optional outside cue:
Donor domain: Tidal prediction
Relation: A repeatable component is predicted from recurring cycles. Actual observations are compared with that expectation, and deviations remain visible rather than being explained away as part of the normal pattern. A useful schedule separates the predictable component from irregular external disturbances.
Boundary: A cyclical prediction alone cannot guarantee the actual state when irregular forces dominate. Local observations, uncertainty, and the age of the estimate remain important.
Treat the relation as an optional prompt for exploration. Transfer useful relationships, not surface nouns. The donor is not evidence that a target intervention will work. Ignore the cue if it cannot support a valid move.

Return JSON only: {"actions":[{"action":"...","mechanism":"...","implementation":"...","check":"...","risk":"..."}],"abstention_reason":""}. Use abstention_reason only to explain an empty action list. No tools or additional research.
